messages.author: 0257010a9dc8ccab
messages.subject: please handle 'ggplot() + c()' more elegantly
parts:
Hi,

Would it be possible to have ggplot2 handle this

ggplot() + c()

by doing nothing rather than giving a cryptic error? It think it
would only take adding an extra case to "+.ggplot" <- function(...)
before the last 'else' block.


6813a6814,6816
> } else if(class(object) == "NULL"){
> set_last_plot(p)
> p


This naturally comes up for example,

add_stuff_to_plot <- function (p, layers=NULL, scales=NULL,
facets=NULL, coord=NULL, options=NULL ){
# do stuff with each of the layers, scales, facets, coord and options...
...
p <- p + layers
...
p <- p + scales
...
}

There may be other ways of doing this (ie only add it if it actually
contains an object), but I don't think this is totally unreasonable as
it is. Depending on the philosophy of the project, I could see either
giving a warning/error that what was passed in was not allowed or
simply assuming the user knew what was going on and do something
sensible (ie just return the cloned ggplot object), but giving the
error

Error in switch(object$class(), layer = { : attempt to apply non-function

is frustrating because it doesn't give much indication about what went
wrong without digging through the ggplot2 code.

Best,
Matt


PS maybe "+.ggplot" could also handle when class(object)== "logical"
more elegantly as well. Thanks!
